What I recommend initiating

Two evidence sets must stay separate. The active CSV has no unresolved ready-to-run source-repair queue. Its 90 residual records describe policy or compatibility boundaries. First repair · P0 Supplemental FIX-01

Stop automatic loss of skills and attributes

The verifier can zero every skill even for an under-cap character with a supported-but-unrecognized cap. The destructive branch is still present in current source.

Why early: protects accumulated player progress. One concentrated behavior, with existing small reproductions.

Effort: medium, despite the localized code. Policy and integration risk are real. No save migration is proposed.

Bound rejected spell output

Why early: stop one demonstrated source of sustained world-object growth before redesigning networking.

Effort: small to medium for the spell only. Expected stability benefit; no measured live speedup or proven incident attribution.

How to read priorities, effort and confidence

P0: data loss, world-load failure, build blocking or network/security risk. P1: crashes, save-corruption risk, global-hook breakage or major player impact. P2: incorrect gameplay, staff hazards or serious doc mismatch. P3: maintainability/minor confusion. P4: organization and future improvement. S04

Priority describes impact, not ease or probability. The CSV supplies no effort, confidence percentage, deadline, or performance estimate. Effort labels and the order in this report are qualitative planning judgments. Confirmed means current source supports the behavior and/or the linked historical fixture reproduced it; no fixtures were rerun for this report.

Raw row order follows generation, not dependencies or an impact/effort sort. Do not restart at row one. Project include drift is IDE hygiene, not a live-runtime failure by itself.

A logical sequence for the next work

Prioritize irreversible loss, then contain an observed growth mechanism, then repair shared invariants. Treat profiling and compatibility coverage as evidence work. Do not turn accepted policy into a bug-fix mandate.

1. Preserve stateFIX-01 + bounded diagnostics
2. Contain outputFIX-05 spell delivery only
3. Fix shared rulesFIX-02–04, then 06/07
4. Measure and provePerformance / save fixtures
5. Optional changePolicy, then organization

This adjusts the October recommendation by pulling the independent, bounded output-containment portion of FIX-05 ahead of the broad shared-policy work. The reason is scope and stability leverage. The network portion of FIX-05 stays behind measurement. S11

FIX-01: make region verification non-destructive

P0 supplemental Localized surface / medium risk

Keep existing skill bases and raw attributes when verification fails. Distinguish real excess, stale cached totals, unsupported caps and profession/origin mismatch. Include the small diagnostic portion of FIX-08 so future failures can be explained.

First scope
PlayerMobile.SkillVerification, its entry contract, and focused test/diagnostic support. Define the narrow guard that prevents additional invalid gains; map the affected grant boundary before coding.
Decision needed
Approve preserving existing points and ordinary travel/login while invalid state is diagnosed and further invalid grants are prevented. Do not silently change origin, caps, profession or restore prior losses from guesses.
Acceptance
Every previously wiping fixture preserves skills and attributes. Unsupported-cap, true-excess, bad-cache and profession cases yield distinct bounded diagnostics. Valid entry remains unchanged; save fields/order remain unchanged.
Scope control
If gain prevention requires the entire transactional redesign, return a separate design batch before widening the patch. Keep NPC initialization, staff restoration and load behavior deliberate.
S11 S12 S14
2

FIX-05a: contain Create Food at the output boundary

P1 supplemental Best bounded stability candidate

Choose an explicit failure policy when the complete spell output cannot be delivered. Preferred proposal: refuse safely or clean up an undeliverable result without leaving new ground objects. Decide mana/reagent/scroll semantics before implementation.

First scope
CreateFoodSpell.OnCast and delivery helper/test support only. Preserve normal outputs and race-specific blood/brain branches. Do not change the global AddToBackpack contract.
Acceptance
Repeat the bounded 25-output fixture: rejected delivery must not accumulate new ground entities. Cover weight and item-count limits, missing/deleted backpack, stacking, partial delivery, all race branches, and normal successful casts.
Risk / limit
Output growth is reproduced; the historical disconnect mechanism is an inference, not a proven live incident. Client behavior and queue-drain timing remain integration work.
Defer
Do not raise the send-queue limit as the “fix,” rewrite all world-item delivery, or delete existing world piles in this batch. Existing pile recovery needs separate evidence and authorization.
S11 S12 S15 S16
3

FIX-02–04: repair the skill accounting contract in small batches

P1 supplemental Shared-system work / larger effort

First agree on one real-total and cap policy, then introduce transactional grants/transfers, then route automatic reward and XML paths through it. Define staff exceptions, player identity, old-save behavior, origin changes and Ether idempotence explicitly.

Why after 1–2
The code spans core setters, origin/cap components, XML and Government rewards. It is not a low-effort blanket setter clamp. Government voting's Forensics reward is disabled in the checked-in baseline, so its bypass is conditional.
Follow-on
Use FIX-06 for individual-cap overshoot and atomic donor loss, and FIX-07 for stale response authorization. Fold those into the agreed grant contract instead of implementing conflicting local policies.
Acceptance
Independent real sum equals accounted total; no grant exceeds chosen caps or violates the approved lock policy; failed transfers lose nothing; repeated completions and stale responses do not duplicate rewards. Existing save format remains compatible.
Decision needed
A specific cross-system gameplay/access policy. Existing “preserve tuning/access” decisions are not permission to change rewards or XML privileges.
S06 S11 S12
4

Measure remaining performance risk and protect save compatibility

Use bounded staging measurements after output containment. Measure object counts, nearby item transmission, queue high-water marks, event subscription counts, save duration and allocations under named scenarios. Keep diagnostics bounded and avoid sensitive account data.

Optimization gate
Choose a specific hot path only after repeatable evidence. Record before/after results on the same workload; preserve packet ordering and behavior. No percentage speedup is claimed by this review.
Compatibility task
For RB-00724, a fixture-only HouseFoundation load/save compatibility project is a useful enabler if housing work is next. Use disposable samples from supported versions; preserve subclass-before-base order. No migration is presently recommended.
Acceptance
A reproducible baseline identifies the bottleneck. Compatibility results specify tested versions and missing data; compile success alone is not save-load proof.
S08 S11 S12 S17
5

Open policy or reorganization work only for a named outcome

Keep staff/access, economy and region rules unchanged unless a new request selects an exact behavior. Put cosmetic moves after stability work. Conditional file-move permission already exists, but each system still needs a plan, evidence updates and rollback.

Batch size
One behavior or one system per reviewable batch. Establish acceptance before coding and validate the touched source, hooks and serialization surfaces.
Defer by default
HouseFoundation normalization, namespace/type renames, mass folder cleanup, global guard sweeps, and speculative network tuning.

Verification, limits and completion gates

This report’s checks

  • Parsed the historical and active CSVs and joined every ID without duplicates or orphans.
  • Counted priority/status combinations and joined 90 gate records to populated executive decisions.
  • Read relevant closeouts and the October skill investigation.
  • Inspected current destructive verifier, spell output/fallback and HouseFoundation serializer paths.
  • Did not run a server, fixture, build, repair, deployment or audit generator.

What future repairs must prove

  • One named behavior, current source evidence, exact file scope and understood policy boundary.
  • Relevant regression cases plus serializer/hook/access review for the touched surfaces.
  • Server source build when applicable and forced runtime script compile for script changes; IDE project builds are a separate check.
  • Disposable save/client staging when required, with the tested versions and limitations recorded.
  • Reviewable diff and rollback instructions before deployment.

The October investigation recorded 335 isolated assertions on its baseline; the logout repair recorded 46. Those are historical verification results, not newly executed checks. Current incident logs, deployment state, live performance, player recovery data and a full world-save/client reproduction were not established here. Do not infer that a recorded pass proves live behavior or that an accepted risk is a new confirmed bug. S10 S12 S13
